product_delta.message: build(entityos): bind security concept into one-file provenance
product_delta.change: EntityOS builder now requires entityos/SECURITY_CONCEPT.md, hashes it, injects SECURITY_CONCEPT_SHA256 into the frozen build identity module, and emits security_concept_sha256 in EntityOSBuildReceipt/v1.

go_cycle_unusual_experiment.name: ONEFILE_RELOCATED_UNICODE_TMPDIR_FOREIGN_CWD
go_cycle_unusual_experiment.executor: EntityOS exact-head self-hosted Linux x64 workflow triggered by this product commit
go_cycle_unusual_experiment.result: PASS; baseline/intervention byte-identical and runtime temporary extraction root empty after exit

external_primary_evidence.finding: onefile mode extracts support files into a temporary runtime directory; POSIX extraction location is selected from TMPDIR/TEMP/TMP then hard-coded fallbacks, so portability and extraction-root authority require explicit tests rather than inferring them from the outer ELF alone.

grf_collapse.hypothesis: The immediate current-head EntityOS provenance gap can be closed by binding the owner-fixed security concept into build identity and rebuilding exact current main.
grf_collapse.counterhypothesis: Rebuilding only changes metadata and does not strengthen product provenance because the security concept remains external documentation.
grf_collapse.discriminator: Require the exact file hash to be consumed by the builder, injected into the frozen build-identity module, emitted in the receipt, then rebuild and execute the exact one-file artifact on the self-hosted Linux x64 lane and locally.
grf_collapse.scope_boundary: This proves build provenance binding, not implementation of first-start permission persistence or destructive-password gating.

remaining_frontier: Current highest-information semantic blocker remains canonical owned Bytes/typed-value admission through WP04 -> ClayExecutableTypedIR/v1 -> the single ClayVM, followed by minimal explicit String/argv process semantics and the remaining network/portability/data/media/visual acceptance gates. Runtime extraction/loading authority remains separately open because outer ELF identity alone does not prove extracted-code ancestry.
negative_results_preserved: Security concept provenance binding is not security-policy implementation.
PyInstaller one-file packaging is not by itself proof of extracted-runtime identity authority.
